name: branchless-select
title: Branchless selection with step and ifElse
summary: Three batteries (18, 42, 86 %) in a loop: red, amber or green fill chosen by step() masks used as paint alpha, a status word picked the same way, and a time estimate chosen by ifElse(left, to-full, charging).
prompt: Show three battery levels from an array; colour each red below 20 %, amber up to 50 % and green above, label it Low/Medium/Good, and show minutes left, or minutes to full when that battery is charging.
teaches: Turn a comparison into a 0/1 mask with step(x, edge), which is x > edge: low = 1 − step(v, 20), mid = step(v, 20) * (1 − step(v, 50)), high = step(v, 50)
Pick a colour by drawing each candidate with its mask as paint alpha: only the one whose mask is 1 shows, with no conditional block
Choose between two numbers with ifElse(otherwise, then, condition): ifElse(v * 6, (100 − v) * 1.2, charging) is the time to full while charging, else the time left
Use max() as a lower bound instead of a branch: the fill is never thinner than 8 px
pitfalls: ifElse takes (else, then, condition), condition LAST: it returns the second argument when the third is > 0, else the first
step(x, edge) is 1 when x > edge, strictly: step(20, 20) = 0, so 20 % counts as Low here
Paint alpha set from a mask stays on the paint: reset {"alpha": 1} before the next solid drawing
Text can't change inside a loop (each label is one text id), so the per-row numbers are drawn outside the loop with arrayGet(@levels, 0…2)

Labels drawn at x = 246 fall off a host narrower than about 330 dp: when the canvas is one composition, scale it as a whole with @fit = min(componentWidth() / 360, componentHeight() / 200) and centre it with a translate

snippets.note: max(37, 29 + 1.16 * level): a minimum width without a branch
one loop draws the three batteries from the levels array

check.describe: Top battery 18 % red, Low, 108 min left; middle 42 % amber, Medium, 69 min to full (charging); bottom 86 % green, Good, 516 min left. Resized, the batteries, percentages and labels are scaled as one (@fit = min(w / 360, h / 200)) and centred: at 234 wide the Low / Medium / Good labels and time estimates stay visible beside smaller batteries; at 540 they are centred at 1:1.
